result.title: Foundation Model Driven Optical Flow
result.comment: 19-pages, 5 figures, 16 tables. Accepted for publication at 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Workshop: RoCo-Spring: The Robust Correspondence Challenge
result.summary: We investigate how frozen pretrained visual and depth representations support dense optical flow when coupled with a supervised matching network. Building on TTSFlow, this paper studies Dense Prediction Transformer (DPT) feature decoding and one coarse-to-fine refinement stage. Our method fuses features from frozen DINOv2 and Depth Anything V2 models and estimates optical flow through a trainable transformer-based matching pipeline. After optical-flow training on FlyingChairs and FlyingThings3D, it achieves 2.37 endpoint error (EPE) on the Sintel training split, Final pass, compared with 2.52 for the FlowSeek (T) configuration reported here. Our RoCo-Spring 2026 entry, RoCo-29.VSAI, obtains a robustness-balanced score of 1.1038, Spring EPE of 1.411, and RobustSpring proxy EPE of 4.739, with a lower balanced score than seven of the twelve listed reference baselines. These results characterize the complete pipeline, which reuses frozen foundation backbones and performs one refinement stage. Code is available at: \url{https://github.com/Visual-and-Spatial-AI-Lab/FFlow}

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究用冻结的 DINOv2 与 Depth Anything V2 特征、经 DPT 解码后接入可训练 transformer 匹配网络，并加一级 coarse-to-fine 细化来做密集光流估计，在 Sintel 与 RoCo-Spring 基准上报告 EPE 等指标。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结视觉/深度表征如何解码保留几何细节」与「coarse-to-fine 迭代细化」或许可为 LVR 中视觉细节是否留在内部状态、latent 状态如何逐级更新提供可核查的方法线索，但论文本身不涉及推理状态使用或证据决策，距离主线较远。
